Updated assessment incorporating the Beige Book: The FOMC statement remains cautiously constructive—solid job gains, moderate growth, subdued inflation around a symmetric 2% objective, and gradual policy normalization (including balance-sheet runoff beginning in October). The July 2017 SLOOS tempers this with weaker demand for CRE (construction/land development/multifamily) and consumer credit (auto/cards), tighter consumer standards, and tighter C&I/CRE standards at foreign banks, partially offset by easing in several mortgage categories and broadly unchanged home-purchase/HELOC standards. The August 2017 Beige Book adds further near-term caution: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria disrupted the energy and natural resources sector, including oil and gas production in the Gulf Coast and Eagle Ford, with noted impacts in the Dallas and Atlanta Districts and mixed agricultural conditions. These point to short-term regional headwinds and temporary energy-related price pressures, consistent with the FOMC’s view that storm effects are transitory. Net effect: still mildly positive but nudged closer to neutral versus the initial read.
